Photo- and Copper Dual-Catalyzed Z‑Selective Chlorosulfonylation
of Allenes for Tetrasubstituted Alkenes
Yaqi Shi, Shichao Hong, Xue Zhang,* Jian Zheng,* and Shengming Ma*
Cite This: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2026, 148, 3259−3269

ABSTRACT: The selectivity control of C�C double bonds,
especially in tetrasubstituted olefins, is a fundamental issue due to
their importance in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, and
material chemistry. Herein, we observed that the stereoselectivity of
chlorosulfonylation of allenoic acids or allenoates was reversed by
applying an organic photocatalyst in combination with a copper
catalyst Cu(acac)
2
, affording Z-selective tetrasubstituted olefins
substituted with a heteroatom of sulfur. This reaction tolerates a
broad range of functional groups. In addition, the intermediate trapping experiment and the reaction of optically active allenoate
confirmed the presence of sulfonyl and allylic radicals. Cyclic voltammetry studies and Stern−Volmer quenching experiments
demonstrated that the reaction proceeds via an oxidative quenching mechanism. Cu(acac)
2
was found to play a crucial role in the
formation of stereodefined π-allyl Cu species in stereoselective chlorosulfonylation.
■
INTRODUCTION
Stereodefined tetrasubstituted alkenes are of significant interest
due to their unique biological, material, and chemical
properties. The distinct biological activities of their Z and E
isomers have been well recognized in medicinal chemistry; for
instance, (E)-clomiphene exhibits antiestrogenic activity,
whereas (Z)-clomiphene displays estrogenic effects (Scheme
1a).
1−3
Fully substituted olefins have been extensively
developed for applications in functional materials, including
photochromic molecular switches and molecular motors.
4,5
Moreover, they serve as versatile molecular scaffolds in organic
synthesis, enabling the construction of complex molecular
architectures.
6−10
Such tetrasubstituted olefins
11−15
have been
traditionally synthesized via the olefination of ketones,
16−18
olefin metathesis,
19
carbometalation of alkynes,
20−27
or
transition metal-catalyzed cross-coupling of preformed stereo-
defined alkenyl halides or their equivalents;
28−30
however, the
challenge is the control of the stereo- and regioselectivity.
These strategies always provide all carbon-substituted
tetrasubstituted olefins. Recently, much attention has been
paid to the stereodefined tetrasubstituted alkenes with a C−B
bond due to the importance of the boron atom in medicinal
chemistry: Song and co-workers developed a copper-catalyzed
borylalkynylation of 1,3-diynes with B
2
pin
2
and bromoacety-
lene, enabling the selective synthesis of boronated phenyl-
diethynylethylene (BPDEE) derivatives.
31
Recently, a practical
stereoselective method for synthesizing fully substituted
stereodefined alkenyl boron compounds via electrophile-
induced 1,2-migration of alkynyl-9-BBN boronates has been
reported by Aggarwal et al.
32
On the other hand, allenes are a class of compounds with
two cumulated C�C bonds, and the functionalization of one
of the two C�C bonds in an allene unit would offer a
potential route to the efficient synthesis of tetrasubstituted
olefins,
33−36
provided that the regio- and stereoselectivity
illustrated in Scheme 1b may be addressed.
37−39
For example,
the electrophilic hydroxylation of allenyl sulfoxides, sulfones,
and phosphine oxides demonstrates an excellent regio- and E-
selectivity based on the electronic effect and the formation of
cyclic intermediates due to the presence of these electron-
withdrawing groups with neighboring group participation
ability (Scheme 1c-1).
40−42
In 2016, we observed that the
conjugated addition of 2,3-allenals with organo zincs afforded
stereodefined fully substituted 2-enals via the concerted 1,5-H
transfer reaction of the conjugated dienol intermediate
(Scheme 1c-2).
43
In 2015, Ba ̈ckvall and his co-workers
elegantly developed a palladium-catalyzed oxidative arylation
of allenes that proceeded with high regio- and stereoselectivity
to afford the tetrasubstituted C�C bond by applying a
carbon−carbon double or triple bond as the coordination
handle (Scheme 1c-3).
44
Another innovative approach to fully
substituted Z-enones has been demonstrated by Chen and his
co-workers using the borylcupration of monosubstituted
allenes and the subsequent reaction with benzoyl chloride.
The stereoselectivity was controlled by the 6-membered chair
form transition state (Scheme 1c-4).
45
On the other hand, the

the major product in 52% yield, and the Z-selective
tetrasubstituted acrylic acid (Z)-3aa was formed in a mere
4% yield (Table 1, entry 1). This is consistent with the fact that
the reactions of 2,3-butadienoic acids would readily undergo
cyclization to afford lactones.

catalytic amount of Pd(OAc)

Subsequent solvent screening indicated that CH
3

by esterification with TMSCHN

CONCLUSION
In summary, a photo/copper dual catalysis has been
established for the chemo-, regio-, and stereoselective
chlorosulfonylation reaction of 2,3-allenoates with sulfonyl
chlorides to afford Z-specific tetrasubstituted alkenes with
sulfonyl group substitution. This protocol accommodates
synthetically useful functional groups such as halogens,
trifluoromethyl, cyano, aldehyde, ketone, sulfone, hydroxyl,
methylthio, and methoxy. It is noted that Cu(acac)
2
is crucial
for stereoselective chlorosulfonylation via the formation of
stereodefined allylic copper intermediates. Cyclic voltammetric
and Stern−Volmer quenching experiments demonstrated that
the excited photocatalyst *4CzIPN was oxidatively quenched
by Cu
II
species. Radical trapping experiments and data on
optically active 2,3-allenoate revealed that sulfonyl and allylic
radicals were generated in this catalytic cycle. Further studies
are being pursued in our laboratory.
